Hi Laura,

Thanks for reaching out and for including me in this process – it's a decision that will clearly have an impact across the whole team, so I'm glad we're thinking it through carefully.

Given everything you've outlined, I think the smaller local gathering combined with virtual sessions is probably the strongest option right now. It feels like the most practical way to balance the budget constraints while still making sure remote employees don't feel like an afterthought. A fully hybrid format sounds appealing in theory, but in my experience those can be tricky to pull off well and often end up feeling a bit disjointed for everyone involved.

In terms of the content, I'd suggest leaning into a mix of social and light professional development activities rather than going too heavily in either direction. That way you're addressing both camps of feedback from last year. Keeping the day shorter and more focused would also likely go down well – I think people appreciated the event more when it didn't feel like a full day commitment with a long commute on either side.

One thing worth considering is whether there's a way to make the virtual component genuinely interactive rather than just a live stream of what's happening in the room. That tends to make a real difference for remote participants.

Happy to discuss any of this further if it would help before you put together your recommendation. Just let me know.

Best,
Mark
